ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has a green shaded triangle, whose base is labeled 16 cm. On the right side of the shaded triangle is a vertical side, and this vertical side also serves as one leg of the right-side pink dashed right triangle. The horizontal base of the right-side dashed right triangle is labeled 9 cm, the hypotenuse is labeled 15 cm, and the figure uses a right-angle symbol to indicate that the vertical side is perpendicular to the horizontal dashed side. Reasoning: The height of the shaded triangle is the length of the vertical side shared with it. In the right-side dashed right triangle, the hypotenuse is 15 cm and the horizontal leg is 9 cm, so use the Pythagorean theorem to find the vertical side: h = sqrt(15^2 - 9^2) = sqrt(225 - 81) = sqrt(144) = 12 cm. The area of the shaded triangle is A = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × 16 × 12 = 96.

method.method_draft: Read the shaded triangle's base as 16 cm from the image. The vertical right side of the shaded triangle is also one leg of the adjacent dashed right triangle; in that dashed right triangle, the horizontal leg is 9 cm and the slanted side is 15 cm. Use the Pythagorean theorem to find the shared vertical height: h = sqrt(15^2 - 9^2) = 12 cm. Then apply the triangle area formula to the shaded triangle: area = (1/2)(16)(12) = 96.
